method: first-edition Fuller primary text plus opposing Dan Taylor primary response plus second-edition self-revision and independent scholarly synthesis

important_deltas.finding: The title and reader copy no longer say Fuller opposed Calvinism in general; the target is the high/hyper-Calvinist inference concerning duty-faith and indiscriminate gospel address.
Dan Taylor 1786 is bound as genuine opposing contemporary primary evidence rather than a secondary mention.
The 1801 second edition is materially revised and cannot be silently back-projected into the 1785 first edition.
The connection between Gospel Worthy and the 1792 missionary society is retained as multicausal rather than a single-book causal claim.

No open Taylor 1786 facsimile was located. The opposition visual is therefore an exact Wellcome institutional catalogue record for the work, explicitly rendered as a catalogue exhibit rather than represented as a title-page scan.

unsupported_popular_claims.claim: Andrew Fuller abandoned Calvinism in Gospel Worthy.
The 1801 wording is identical to the 1785 first edition.
Gospel Worthy alone caused the Baptist Missionary Society to be founded.
The Wellcome Taylor catalogue record is a facsimile of the 1786 title page.

claim_upgrade_conditions.claim: specific doctrinal wording assigned to the 1785 first edition
claim_upgrade_conditions.upgrade_requires: locator in the 1785 text rather than the 1801 corrected edition

claim_upgrade_conditions.claim: direct causal statement from Gospel Worthy to BMS foundation
claim_upgrade_conditions.upgrade_requires: near-contemporary participant document explicitly making that causal connection
an openly retrievable institutional or archival image/PDF demonstrably containing the 1786 edition page

visual_plan.concept: Wellcome institutional catalogue record for Dan Taylor's 1786 Observations, rendered as a catalog-record exhibit and explicitly not a facsimile
